chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that

the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about a baby lamb that had been nourished with the milk of a female pig. So he said: 'Confine it and feed it oilseed cake, date kernels, barley, and bread, if it has become independent of the milk. But if it has not become independent of the milk, then place it on the udder of a sheep for seven days; then its flesh may be eaten.'

key_terms.اسْتَغْنَى عَنِ اللَّبَن: Became independent of milk — i.e., weaned; the key jurisprudential condition determining the purification method
key_terms.الْكُسْب: Oilseed cake — pressed residue from oil-producing seeds, used as animal fodder
key_terms.حَمَل: Baby lamb or baby goat — a young nursing animal, the subject of the jurisprudential question
key_terms.خِنْزِيرَة: Female pig/sow — whose milk is najis (ritually impure), tainting the animal fed on it
key_terms.ضَرْع شَاة: Udder of a sheep — the halal nursing source used for ritual purification over seven days

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating a baby animal raised on pig's milk according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling (fatwa) from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) — transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq through the al-Sakuni chain — concerning the ritual permissibility of eating a young animal that was raised on pig's milk. In classical Shia jurisprudence, consuming pig products renders an animal ritually impure (najis), and this hadith provides a purification protocol: if the animal is weaned, feed it clean food; if still nursing, attach it to a sheep's udder for seven days to purify its body before slaughter.
